correctness.rationale: Chen et al. Corollary 5.4 supplies the exact full-dimensional original-coordinate halfspaces. The integer bidiagonal transform reduces them to suffix-normal box bounds and oriented unit-normal path inequalities. The Chebyshev LP has upper bounds from every directed path with endpoint weights sqrt(n-i+1), and a direct longest-path potential attains the maximum-run barrier, establishing both directions for all n>=2. Equality enforces all claimed active constraints; separate extremal-word and affine-unimodular arguments verify the sharp range and Ehrhart pair. An independently constructed scipy HiGHS LP checked all 1,023 orientation words through n=10, including 36,868 shifted inequalities; 72 paired binary vertices were also tested. Finite tests corroborate but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The original linked-snake paper states suffix facets, linked-toric classification, triangulations and volumes, not the metric run obstruction. Full published mathematical comparisons distinguish generalized snake order polytopes, signed order polytopes, and marked order polytopes by their defining objects and facet-normal metrics. Neither the accessible primary theorem nor the compared published claims implies the sqrt-suffix weighted run classification, its sharp word-dependent extrema, or the explicit Ehrhart-equivalent unequal-radius pair. Residual risk remains for an unindexed geometric reformulation.
residual_risks: Unindexed or older publications could contain the same exact weighted-run metric formula under different terminology.
The generic longest-path feasibility method is standard; originality here is limited to the specific full linked-snake metric classification and its consequences.
The compared chainlink record was not inspected in full; its identified cyclic-chainlink object and parameters differ, but inaccessible variants remain possible.

value.rationale: The linked symmetric snake family is a natural complete 2^(n-1)-parameter subfamily of a newly studied type-C matroid-polytope construction. The theorem replaces continuous Euclidean inball optimization by a run maximum computable in linear time, gives every center and a constructive attaining center, shows sharp n^-1 versus n^-1/2 inradius scales, and gives an infinite explicit unimodular/Ehrhart-equivalent but nonisometric pair. None of these conclusions is merely a parameter substitution into the cited standard-coordinate poset results. No broad downstream theorem is claimed.
